name: PersonQA
intro: PersonQA 是 OpenAI 系统卡披露、但没有独立论文的内部人物事实问答评测。它以公开可得的人物事实覆盖 18 类事实，报告已尝试答案准确率与幻觉率；样本量、类别名称、构建、标注、提示词、评分器、数据和代码均未公开。
build_method: 内部人物事实问答, 18类事实, 构建与标注流程未披露
eval_feature: 已尝试答案准确率, 幻觉率, 18类人物事实, 金标时效性风险
scale: 18类人物事实, 样本总量未公开
build_method_en: Internal person-fact QA, 18 fact categories, construction and annotation process not disclosed
eval_feature_en: Attempted-answer accuracy, hallucination rate, 18 person-fact categories, stale-reference risk
intro_en: PersonQA is an internal person-fact QA evaluation disclosed in OpenAI system cards, with no standalone paper. It covers 18 categories of publicly available facts about people and reports attempted-answer accuracy plus hallucination rate. OpenAI has not released its item count, category names, construction, annotation, prompt, grader, data, or code.
scale_en: 18 person-fact categories; total item count not disclosed

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_stage=paper-and-official-release audit; scope=PersonQA only. PersonQA does not have a standalone paper, a public repository, or a public dataset. The source hierarchy therefore uses fixed official OpenAI system-card PDFs and does not promote a marketing page, a later benchmark adaptation, or a third-party reconstruction into a missing benchmark paper. Fixed source 1 is the December 5, 2024 OpenAI o1 System Card at https://cdn.openai.com/o1-system-card-20241205.pdf, SHA256 3ba7bdbe69e022f6be0527edbfe18ac1becdea48d5be9891ab764ff336c8a033. Its PersonQA section states only that the benchmark contains questions and publicly available facts about people, measures model accuracy on attempted answers, and reports accuracy and hallucination rate; it defines accuracy as whether the model answered correctly and hallucination rate as how often the model hallucinated. Fixed source 2 is the February 25, 2025 Deep Research System Card at https://cdn.openai.com/deep-research-system-card.pdf, SHA256 6662a84c7fdffc19ddecf969a7f00ba6216d7542b2dd9becd5354d6273da8f5a. This card adds the only verified scale fact used in the graph: PersonQA contains 18 categories of facts about people. It also reports a post-hoc audit in which the test set was out of date for some questions; a model could correctly name more children than the stale reference, causing the displayed hallucination rate to overstate actual hallucination. The card says future versions need more careful answer examination. Fixed source 3 is the April 16, 2025 OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card at https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/2221c875-02dc-4789-800b-e7758f3722c1/o3-and-o4-mini-system-card.pdf, SHA256 32d7ca19fff2ed0dc2d06f84e3143900bbd7898bb6f443c094477fb4ce0fc4ab. It repeats the task and metric definitions and records an interpretation boundary: o3 made more claims overall, leading to more accurate claims and more inaccurate or hallucinated claims, while the cause was not established. These three cards report different model snapshots and tables, so the graph does not merge their scores into one immutable run or claim a universal checkpoint. Construction boundary: OpenAI does not disclose the 18 category names, category distribution, item count, person count, question count, source inventory, source-selection rules, collection date, refresh cadence, question-authoring procedure, reference-answer authoring, annotator identity or qualifications, independent review, adjudication, quality-control statistics, train/validation/test splits, or item schema. Evaluation boundary: OpenAI does not disclose the PersonQA system or user prompt, parser, correctness grader, hallucination grader, generation settings, number of samples or attempts, refusal and abstention handling, the exact attempted-answer denominator, the hallucination unit, or aggregation formulas beyond the short metric descriptions. No such implementation is inferred from SimpleQA or from unrelated OpenAI eval repositories. Release boundary: the official sources do not link a PersonQA dataset, code repository, item payload, license, leaderboard, or downloadable evaluation bundle. Consequently no public Git commit or public data revision can be recorded; this honest absence of a public release is not replaced by a fabricated hash and does not claim that internal revisions or hashes do not exist. The PDF hashes above pin the evidence that actually exists. The main solid path is deliberately narrow: disclosed task definition, 18-category internal set, card-specific model response, attempted-answer scope, accuracy and hallucination metrics, paired reporting, then the documented freshness audit. Dashed callouts preserve source, construction, evaluation, release, and interpretation boundaries and every secondary edge explicitly renders dashed. The English and Chinese specs have identical IDs, semantic node types, positions, edges, waypoints, and modules. English labels contain no Chinese text; Chinese labels retain the same meaning without inventing category names, prompts, parsers, judges, human workflows, or release artifacts. The fallback Mermaid strings are regenerated exactly from the two canonical YAML specs. Formal Draw.io, arch, SVG, and PNG assets are intentionally unchanged during this source stage. Formal publication evidence [site-a12f-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2030×705 (English) and 2021×705 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2028×703 and 2019×703. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
